name: Chianti Classico

communes: San Casciano In Val Di Pesa

terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
The original heartland of an Italian wine area. Every bottle of Chianti Classico carries the black rooster on its neck seal.
keyfacts: Chianti Classico is a Tuscan DOCG made from 80 to 100% Sangiovese, with other red grapes allowed up to a maximum of 20%.
Chianti Classico became its own denomination in 1996 and is no longer a subzone of Chianti.
The symbol of the Lega del Chianti, a black rooster on a gold field, became the emblem of the Chianti Classico consortium.
Riserva needs at least two years of aging, including at least three months in bottle, and a minimum total alcohol of 12.5%.

notes: Chianti Classico is medium bodied, with firm tannin and medium-high to high acidity.
Riserva must age at least 24 months at the winery.

blurb.text: A Tuscan DOCG whose rules cover communes such as Castellina, Gaiole, Greve and Radda in Chianti.
